newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO CHAIRMAN TO TAKE FIFA TO COURT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO CHAIRMAN TO TAKE FIFA TO COURT.

text.p: Deportivo Coruna chairman Augusto Lendoiro said on Tuesday that he would take officials of the Spanish Football Federation and FIFA to court.
"(FIFA) have violated the European agreement for the protection of human rights and fundamental liberties by preventing my access to the tribunals of justice," said Lendoiro.
On Monday, FIFA rejected Lendoiro's appeal against an 18-month suspension and a fine of 100,000 Swiss francs ($68,600) which they imposed as punishment for taking the Spanish federation to court.
Lendoiro had incurred FIFA's wrath by obtaining a court injunction against a one-game home ban imposed by the Spanish federation after a coin was thrown at a referee during a league match.
Lendoiro said he would take the new action at a personal level. FIFA bylaws forbid teams from taking recourse in civil courts.
"Deportivo for obvious reasons can't do so because of the risks that would be run," he said.
FIFA said on Monday that Lendoiro remained suspended from all soccer activities until August 1998.
